threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think waiting for a bus means you won't see ten cyclists zoom past. In Dalston, it's like a race you didn't sign up for.
Caught a couple arguing about which curry house was best, then the bus driver chimed in with his go-to spot. Only in Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when the kebab shop owner remembered my order. It’s the little things, like seeing the same stray cat sunbathing on my balcony every afternoon.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find spontaneous parties in abandoned buildings with art installations, where the music complements the graffiti on the walls.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local knows how to dodge the BART delays like it's an Olympic sport—gotta time those transfers to the bus just right.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus where a guy was trying to barter his homemade kombucha for a ride. Only in The Haight, I guess.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all Gràcia residents live in bohemian bliss. Most of us are just hustling to pay rent and navigate the noisy, never-ending fiestas.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they enthusiastically stand on the wrong side of the escalator, blocking locals rushing to get to work.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the tube' can get you anywhere. The bus routes here are the real lifeline, mate.
Caught a woman singing to herself on the 196. She was convinced it was a private concert—everyone else just pretended not to notice.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One afternoon I saw a neighbor watering their plants while their cat lazily watched a pigeon steal a croissant from the doorstep. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you can buy a currywurst from a stand while a techno DJ spins records right beside you—only in Berlin can street food and nightlife collide like this.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they instinctively dodge the skateboarders on Valencia while holding a taco, like it’s an Olympic sport.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full suit dance on the 47 like it was his personal stage this morning. Only in SF do we mix commuting with Broadway.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the Plaza, but the real charm is in the hidden alleys where locals gather for sunny vermut on a Tuesday.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by the way they fumble with the T-10 card at the metro, as if it’s a rare treasure instead of a simple transit pass.
